svg.text: Raspberry Pi 4 · DHT22 · ADS1115 · MQ-135 · LDR module · 5 V relay module · 12 V fan. Tags show where each wire lands on the Pi (physical pin numbers).
40-pin GPIO header along the top edge, pin 1 at the left
• MQ-135 runs on 5 V: never wire its AO or DO straight to the Pi. AO → R1 10 kΩ → A0, and R2 20 kΩ from A0 to GND.
• ADS1115 ADDR to GND sets I²C address 0x48. Turn on I²C: sudo raspi-config nonint do_i2c 0, then reboot.
• No ADS1115? Use DO pins instead: MQ-135 DO → GPIO 17 (pin 11) through the same 10k/20k divider; LDR DO → GPIO 27 (pin 13).
• Fan uses the relay's NO + COM contacts, so it's off whenever the Pi is off. Mains fans need a mains-rated relay and an enclosure.
• Any GND pin works (6, 9, 14, 20, 25, 30, 34, 39). Bare 4-pin DHT22: add 10 kΩ from DATA to 3.3 V.
